title: Universe naturality of strict-diagram rectification and cocones
statement:
Fix nested Grothendieck universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P=(B,S,\{K_a^{\triangleleft}\to B\})$ be a $\mathcal U$-small categorical pattern of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], with all $2$-simplices scaled and every $K_a$ having finitely many nondegenerate simplices (the empty shape is allowed). Write $\mathsf M_{P,\mathcal W}$ for the marked pattern model category of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] in universe $\mathcal W$, and $\iota$ for inclusion of the smaller marked simplicial objects into the larger ones. Use the common generators, weak equivalences and fibrant replacements of [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison].

Use coherent nerves and realizations from [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], the localization comparison from [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], and rectification of strict enriched diagrams from [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams]. Put $\mathcal C_{\mathcal W}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathsf M_{P,\mathcal W}^{\mathrm{cf}})$, formed in an auxiliary universe containing both collections of objects. Inclusion of bifibrant objects gives a coherent functor $j:\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal C_{\mathcal U'}$.

Let $K$ be a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set and $u:\mathfrak C[K]\to I$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence to a $\mathcal U$-small locally Kan simplicial category. Then $u$ is still a Dwyer--Kan equivalence in $\mathcal U'$. For every enriched $F:I\to\mathsf M_{P,\mathcal U}$, let $p:K\to\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$ be its coherent diagram under the localization and rectification comparisons. The same strict enriched diagram, included into the larger category, corresponds to $j\circ p$. This comparison is natural on the entire functor infinity categories, including coherent transformations.

If $t:F\to\Delta_I A$ is an enriched cocone with $A$ in $\mathsf M_{P,\mathcal U}$, its coherent cocone is carried by $j$ to the coherent cocone obtained from the included $t$. Objectwise weak equivalences used in presenting $F$ and weak-equivalence fibrant replacements of $A$ are respected by this comparison. No colimit hypothesis on $t$ is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4, Remark 4.2.4.5 and Theorem 4.2.4.1, printed pp.257-259; evaluation-induced rectification and cocone comparison. Combined with Higher Algebra, Construction 1.3.4.18 and Theorem 1.3.4.20, printed pp.116-117. The explicit universe naturality is agent-written; no Stacks tag states it.

proof.text: All set constructions below use the same representatives in the two universes. A function between two $\mathcal U$-sets already belongs to $\mathcal U$: its graph is a subset of their product. Likewise all subsets, countable unions and quotients of these sets are available there. In the realization formula of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the simplex sets, real simplices, equivalence relation and quotient topology are therefore unchanged. The functions defining paths, based cubes and their homotopies, and the continuity tests on subsets, are unchanged as well. Thus a map of smaller simplicial sets is a weak homotopy equivalence in one universe exactly when it is in the other. The mapping sets and composition laws of $\mathfrak C[K]$ and $I$ are unchanged: the former is the colimit of the fixed simplex thickenings over the smaller category of simplices. Apply the definition of Dwyer--Kan equivalence in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Its local weak-equivalence tests and its component categories are identical, including the functions witnessing an equivalence of those categories. Hence the given $u$ remains a Dwyer--Kan equivalence; the horn-filling definition also keeps $I$ locally Kan.

source.place: Definitions 1.1.5.1 and 1.1.5.5; universe absoluteness expanded from the stated set constructions.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] every pattern object is cofibrant, since its initial map is an underlying monomorphism. By [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison] the smaller fibrant objects remain fibrant. For two smaller objects $X,Y$ the formula $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf M_P}(X\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Y)$ involves exactly the same functions, simplicial identities, marking tests and equations over $B$ in both universes. Its operators are precomposition, and composition is composition of these functions. The inclusion of bifibrant objects is consequently a full simplicial functor. Its coherent nerve is the specified $j$, by the definition of $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. This compares the actual sharp mapping sets, before any passage to homotopy categories.

source.place: Theorem B.0.20 and Definition B.2.1; degreewise comparison of the displayed sharp enrichment.

proof.text: Let $J$ be any $\mathcal U$-small locally Kan simplicial category, and write $D_{\mathcal W}(J)=\mathsf M_{P,\mathcal W}^{J}$ with its projective model structure from [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. The hypotheses of [lem-coef-projective-diagram-universe-cofibrancy] are exactly ours: the same $\mathcal U$-small pattern $P$ with scaled $2$-simplices and finite cone shapes, and a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial category with small object set and Kan mapping sets. That node states that the inclusion $D_{\mathcal U}(J)\to D_{\mathcal U'}(J)$ sends every projective cofibration between smaller diagrams to a projective cofibration, and every projectively cofibrant-fibrant diagram to a projectively cofibrant-fibrant one. Its proof supplies both directions of the free-generator argument: a smaller cell presentation by the common generators $F_i(g)$, $F_i(X)(k)=J(i,k)\otimes X$ with $T\otimes X=X\times T^\sharp$, remains a cell presentation, and each $F_i(g)$ lifts against objectwise trivial fibrations. We apply it to $J=I$ and, in step 9, to the terminal extension of step 7, which are both locally Kan and $\mathcal U$-small.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.5, free-diagram projective generators; explicit degreewise preservation of smaller cell presentations.

proof.text: Projective fibrancy is objectwise, and projective weak equivalences are objectwise by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams]. The comparison [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison] therefore preserves and reflects both properties on smaller diagrams. Together with step 3 this gives an inclusion $d_J:D_{\mathcal U}(J)^{cf}\to D_{\mathcal U'}(J)^{cf}$. This is a simplicial inclusion, not merely an ordinary functor. Namely [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-size-generation] describes each mapping $n$-simplex as a family $E_i\otimes\Delta^n\to H_i$ commuting with the $J$-actions. The object set of $J$ is smaller; all families belong to the same smaller product of function sets, and their naturality equations are identical. Thus the two enriched ends are the same simplicial set, with the same componentwise composition.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2; enriched diagram mapping ends and objectwise projective fibrations and weak equivalences.

proof.text:
Take $J=I$, and put $v:K\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}I$ equal to the adjoint of $u$. Evaluation on projectively bifibrant diagrams lands in bifibrant model objects by [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. The rectification map $e_{\mathcal W}:N_{\mathrm{hc}}D_{\mathcal W}(I)^{cf}\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C_{\mathcal W})$ is exactly the evaluation-induced equivalence in [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification]. Concretely it is adjoint to the composite of $v$ with the nerve of enriched evaluation $I\times D_{\mathcal W}(I)^{cf}\to\mathsf M_{P,\mathcal W}^{cf}$. The coherent nerve preserves this product: a functor from each simplex thickening into a product is a pair of functors. Steps 2 and 4 show that both routes round the evaluation square send $(i,E)$ to the same $E_i$, and send a pair of mapping simplices to the same composite of an action map and a component of an enriched transformation. These are identities of simplicial maps. Adjunction therefore gives
$$e_{\mathcal U'}N_{\mathrm{hc}}(d_I)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,j)e_{\mathcal U}.$$
The identity holds on every simplex of the coherent nerve and hence includes all coherent transformations and their higher compatibilities, not just the objects of the diagram categories.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4 and Remark 4.2.4.5, the comparison induced by evaluation; its degreewise naturality is expanded here.

proof.text: The ordinary inclusion $\iota_I:D_{\mathcal U}(I)\to D_{\mathcal U'}(I)$ preserves objectwise weak equivalences by step 4, so it induces a functor of infinity localizations. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] to both diagram model categories and to the two pattern model categories. Its inverse comparison on bifibrant objects agrees with ordinary inclusion followed by localization. Consequently $N_{\mathrm{hc}}d_I$ is the functor induced by $\iota_I$ under those comparisons: precompose both candidates with the localization of the ordinary bifibrant subcategory; the resulting functors agree on the ordinary inclusion, and that subcategory induces an equivalence of localizations. The full functor-category universal property in the cited node extends this agreement to a coherent natural equivalence. The identical argument for pattern objects identifies the induced localization functor with $j$. Transporting step 5 along these equivalences proves the claimed square on the entire localized diagram categories. Thus any strict $F$, without a fibrancy or cofibrancy hypothesis, has included presentation corresponding to $j\circ p$. This uses the universal property for functor infinity categories, rather than only the ordinary homotopy-category property.

source.place: Construction 1.3.4.18, Theorem 1.3.4.20 and Remark 1.3.4.16; formal application of the entire-functor-category localization property.

proof.text: Encode the particular enriched cocone $t:F\to\Delta_I A$ as one strict enriched diagram $H:J\to\mathsf M_{P,\mathcal U}$. Here $J$ is obtained from $I$ by adjoining an object $*$, with $J(i,*)=J(*,*)=\Delta^0$ and $J(*,i)=\varnothing$ for $i\in I$; the other mapping sets are those of $I$. Composition involving $*$ is the unique possible map. Set $H|_I=F$, $H(*)=A$, and let the unique vertex of $J(i,*)$ act as $t_i$. The enriched functor equations are precisely the naturality equations of $t$, so this encoding is valid also for empty $I$. The new index is smaller and locally Kan. Restriction of projectively cofibrant $J$-diagrams to $I$ preserves cofibrancy: a generator based at $i\in I$ restricts to the same free $I$-generator, whereas a generator based at $*$ restricts to the identity of the initial $I$-diagram, since $J(*,i)=\varnothing$. Restriction preserves the cell operations and retracts because the colimits are objectwise, so a projectively cofibrant $J$-diagram restricts to a retract of a relative cell complex of free $I$-generators $F_i(g)$ with $g$ in the common generating set. Such a complex is projectively cofibrant: by the free-diagram adjunction of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], a lifting problem of $F_i(g)$ against $D\to D'$ is one of $g$ against its component at $i$, and projective trivial fibrations are objectwise trivial fibrations, so $F_i(g)$ lies in the left lifting class. That class is closed under pushouts and retracts by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] and under transfinite composites by [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]; a coproduct of members lifts summand by summand. It also preserves projective fibrancy and weak equivalences, since these are objectwise.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2; elementary adjoining-terminal-object encoding of an enriched natural transformation to a constant diagram.

proof.text: Use functorial projective factorizations in the smaller $D_{\mathcal U}(J)$ to obtain $H\xleftarrow{\sim}QH\xrightarrow{\sim}BH$, with $QH$ cofibrant and $BH$ bifibrant. First factor the initial map as a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration, then factor $QH\to1$ as a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration. By step 7, $BH|_I$ is projectively bifibrant; its apex $BH(*)$ is bifibrant by the evaluation assertion in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. The structure maps to $*$ give an enriched transformation $BH|_I\to\Delta_I BH(*)$. It gives an enriched functor $I\times[1]\to\mathsf M_{P,\mathcal U}^{cf}$: on the cross arrows use that transformation, whose naturality is exactly the composition condition. Its coherent nerve, pulled back along $v\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}$, is a simplex $K\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C_{\mathcal U}$, the required actual coherent cocone. Here $[1]$ has discrete mapping sets, so its coherent nerve is $\Delta^1$. The counit $\mathfrak C[N_{\mathrm{hc}}J]\to J$ is Dwyer--Kan by [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification], since $J$ is locally Kan. Use it for rectification on $J$. The localization comparison then identifies the evaluated $BH$ with $H$. Restrict along $I\times[1]\to J$, sending $(i,0)$ to $i$ and $(i,1)$ to $*$, and evaluate at $*$: these operations retain the actual legs and apex and identify this cocone with the one presented by $t$. They commute with evaluation by composition of the same enriched functors. It is not necessary to apply a non-enriched replacement objectwise to an enriched functor.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2 and Proposition 4.2.4.4; evaluation of a replacement of the entire enriched cocone. Compare Higher Algebra, Theorem 1.3.4.20.

proof.text: Apply steps 3--6 also to the smaller index $J$ of step 7. The same $BH$ is bifibrant in the larger projective category, and the same two arrows of its replacement zigzag are objectwise weak equivalences there. The enriched functor $I\times[1]\to\mathsf M_P^{cf}$ of step 8 has exactly the same objects, action maps and transformation components after inclusion, by step 2. Its coherent nerve therefore becomes its composite with $j$, as does its pullback along $v\times\mathrm{id}$. This proves the assertion about the actual cocone represented by the included $t$. If either universe uses another presentation, step 6 gives the same coherent natural comparison after localization, so the conclusion is independent of those presentation choices. Finally the common natural isomorphism $\iota R_{\mathcal U}\cong R_{\mathcal U'}\iota$ from [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison] carries the specified apex replacement map $A\to RA$ to its larger-universe replacement map. Naturality of $t$ under postcomposition carries its legs to $F_i\to A\to RA$ on both sides. Every objectwise weak equivalence in a presentation is inverted on both sides by the same localization square. The constant diagram remains constant since every action is an identity, so its image is exactly the constant coherent diagram at $j(RA)$. No assertion that a cocone is colimiting is used in any of these constructions.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20 and the common replacement comparison of lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison; direct evaluation of the cocone legs.
